In grammar , the voice (or diathesis ) of a verb describes the relationship between the action (or state) that the verb expresses and the participants identified by its arguments (subject, object, etc.). [ 1 ] When the subject is the agent or doer of the action, the verb is in the active voice . When the subject is the patient, target or undergoer of the action, the verb is said to be in the passive voice . [ 2 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] When the subject both performs and receives the action expressed by the verb, the verb is in the middle voice.
